texts: Most patients with tricuspid atresia present with cyanosis in the first day of life: A.
Systemic venous blood mixes with pulmonary venous blood in the left atrium, and in most patients flow to the lungs is restricted by a small VSD or pulmonary stenosis.
Cyanosis deepens as the ductus closes; the few with unrestricted lung flow have mild cyanosis and heart failure, worsening as pulmonary vascular resistance falls.
The ECG classically shows left-axis deviation and large P waves.
In the picture, on day one the baby's lips are already blue.
Memory hook: a welded trident turns the lips blue on day one.
